data.one_liner: Create, sign, and send API requests to AWS services with Signature Version 4.
data.what_it_does: Allows Dart and Flutter applications to communicate with AWS services by automatically handling Signature Version 4 signing for HTTP requests. Supports custom endpoints, query parameters, headers, and mock requests for testing.
use_when: You need to call AWS REST APIs directly without bringing in the full official AWS SDK.
You need to handle AWS Signature Version 4 signing manually for custom or lightweight API calls.
avoid_when: You require automatic retries, exponential backoff, or persistent connection pooling out of the box.
You want a fully-featured official AWS SDK with generated models for all AWS services.
strengths: Simple API to create, sign, and send requests using AWS SigV4.
Supports custom endpoints, LocalStack, and mock requests for testing.
weaknesses: Does not implement automatic retries or built-in connection pooling.
Lacks full high-level service client wrappers compared to complete AWS SDKs.
data.setup_notes: On Android, add the internet permission `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />` to AndroidManifest.xml.

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need a standard HTTP client without built-in AWS Signature Version 4 request signing.

alternatives.name: dio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need interceptors, global configuration, and advanced HTTP client features.
